answers.value: Statement II alone settles it (every qualifying total contains a 5); Statement I alone does not, because 32 = 2+10+20 is non-prime and has no 5
answers.reasoning: Read as printed: X gets three coins whose denominations are three DIFFERENT values drawn from 1, 2, 5, 10, 20. The ten possible totals are 8, 13, 23, 16, 26, 31, 17, 27, 32, 35. Statement I (m not prime) leaves 8, 16, 26, 27, 32, 35 — of these 32 = 2+10+20 has no 5 while the rest do, so I alone cannot decide. Statement II (digit sum of m greater than 5) leaves 8, 16, 26, 17, 27, 35 (digit sums 8, 7, 8, 8, 9, 8), and every one of those six totals contains the 5-coin; the four excluded totals 13, 23, 31, 32 have digit sums 4, 5, 4, 5. So II alone answers YES and I alone does not, which is exactly option A.

answers.value: Neither statement alone nor both together fix which of x and y is bigger
answers.reasoning: Statement I alone fails: with x = 0.5, y = 0.3 satisfies 0.25 < 0.3 < 1 and gives x > y, while y = 0.9 satisfies it and gives y > x. Statement II alone fails: with x = 0.25 (so sqrt(x) = 0.5), y = 0.1 gives x > y and y = 0.4 gives y > x, both satisfying y < sqrt(x) < 1. Together the conditions reduce to x^2 < y < sqrt(x) with 0 < x < 1, and since x^2 < x < sqrt(x) on that interval, x itself lies strictly inside the permitted band for y — x = 0.25 with y = 0.1 and with y = 0.4 both satisfy BOTH statements yet give opposite answers. Hence the question cannot be answered even using both.

answers.value: Both statements together prove x is even; neither alone does
answers.reasoning: Statement I says x^2 y^2 = (xy)^2 is even, so xy is even, meaning x or y is even — x = 1, y = 2 satisfies it with x odd, so I alone is not enough. Statement II says 1 + x^2 + y^2 is odd, so x^2 + y^2 is even, so x and y have the same parity — both odd (x = y = 1) or both even (x = y = 2), so II alone is not enough. Combining them: if x and y were both odd, x^2 y^2 would be odd, contradicting I; so both must be even, and x is even. Both together suffice, neither alone does.

answers.value: Both statements only force every member of T to have the same parity; they never distinguish an all-odd T from an all-even T
answers.reasoning: Statement I says the sum of any two members of T is even, which happens exactly when all members share a parity — so T is entirely odd (all from X) or entirely even (all from Y), and I alone cannot say which. Statement II says (p-1)q is even for any p, q drawn from T; a mixed T fails this (take p even and q odd, then p-1 and q are both odd and the product is odd), but an all-odd T passes (p-1 is even) and an all-even T also passes (q is even), so II alone likewise only proves homogeneity. Since both statements deliver the identical conclusion, combining them adds nothing and the all-odd case is never ruled out. The question therefore cannot be answered even with both.

A fourth plane adds exactly as many pieces as it passes through, and a single plane can meet at most 6 of the 8 blocks of a 2x2x2 arrangement, so from x3 = 8 the ceiling is 14; independently, four planes can divide a convex solid into at most 15 regions. In the second weighing put one of those three against another: if they balance the third is light, otherwise the higher one is. A single weighing has only three possible outcomes and so can single out at most three candidates, which is fewer than seven, so one attempt cannot guarantee identification. Two is therefore the minimum that works with certainty.

Every tile is 3 feet wide and the strip is 3 feet wide, so the problem reduces to writing 100 as 3a + 7b + 11c. For n tiles the covered length is at least 3n, and each larger tile adds an excess of 4 feet (the 7-footer) or 8 feet (the 11-footer), so 100 - 3n must be a sum of 4s and 8s. n = 33 would need an excess of 1 and is impossible, while n = 32 needs 4, achieved by thirty-one 3-foot tiles and one 7-foot tile, so the maximum x is 32. For the minimum, 11n - 100 must likewise be a sum of 4s and 8s: n = 10 leaves 10 and n = 11 leaves 21, neither a multiple of 4, whereas n = 12 leaves 32 = 4 x 8, achieved by eight 11-foot tiles and four 3-foot tiles, so the minimum y is 12. Hence x - y = 20. (Requiring all three sizes to appear would give 28 - 12 = 16, which is not among the options, confirming that no such requirement is intended.)
